title: Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act / Scheme
summary: any rural household whose adult members volunteer for unskilled manual work; demand-driven; unemployment allowance if work not given within 15 days Imbert & Papp (AEJ Applied 2015): early-phase districts show public hiring crowded out private work and raised private-sector wages; welfare gains to the poor from the wage rise are large relative to gains to participants alone Muralidharan, Niehaus & Sukhtankar (AER 2016), AP Smartcards RCT over 157 subdistricts/19 mn people: faster, more predictable, less corrupt NREGS payments; significant leakage reduction; no loss of access; time savings alone covered cost CAG performance audit (2013) found fall in employment, only 30.3% of planned works completed, planning norms unmet in a third of GPs (as summarised by Wikipedia pointer) Lokniti-CSDS 2024 post-poll (N=19,663): 33.7% of households report MGNREGA benefit in last 5 years; of these 63.5% credit the central government, 27.0% the state MoRD, Jul 2025: 99.79% of eligible households offered work against demand in FY 2025-26 (to 22 Jul 2025) — the government's rebuttal to 'cut' narratives Critics (NREGA Sangharsh Morcha via BehanBox): 60:40 sharing could shift ~₹55,000 cr to states; caps on state fund requests introduced 2025; digital attendance excluded workers Widely credited by political scientists as a contributor to UPA's improved 2009 performance, but the 38-month gap between launch and that election makes a narrow 'pre-poll bribe' reading weak; the innocent reading (a multi-year employment guarantee, not a pre-poll cash drop) fits the timeline better. Muralidharan, Niehaus & Sukhtankar (NBER 23838; Econometrica 2023), randomised at sub-district scale in Andhra Pradesh: improving NREGS implementation raised beneficiary households' earnings by 14% and cut poverty by 26%; 86% of income gains came from non-programme earnings via higher private wages and employment — a general-equilibrium gain invisible in programme-only accounting. Same authors (AER 2016), RCT over 157 subdistricts and 19 million people: biometric Smartcard payments made NREGS payments faster, more predictable and less corrupt, reduced leakage in NREGS and social-security pensions without reducing access; time savings alone covered the cost. Deshpande, Tillin & Kailash (2019, NES 2019): MGNREGA and pension recipients were less likely to vote BJP, while Ujjwala/Jan Dhan/Awas recipients were more likely; MGNREGA, a Congress-era scheme, is now more associated with the central government than before. Bihar RCT (Banerjee, Duflo, Imbert, Mathew & Pande 2020): a fund-flow/e-governance reform in MGNREGA reduced leakage — reported findings not re-read in this sweep (Crossref metadata only). Bihar RCT (Muralidharan, Niehaus, Sukhtankar & Weaver 2021): phone-based monitoring of MGNREGA improved last-mile delivery — findings not re-read in this sweep. Andhra Pradesh (Muralidharan, Niehaus & Sukhtankar 2016, 2023): biometric smartcard payments and improved NREGS implementation raised wages and had general-equilibrium effects on rural labour markets — findings not re-read in this sweep. MoRD (PIB 2023-02-03) rebutted the ‘18% cut’ reading: MGNREGA is demand-driven and actual releases have exceeded BE every year since 2014-15; the West Bengal fund stoppage under s.27 is not addressed in either PIB release opened.

summary: married/widowed/divorced/abandoned women aged 21-60, household income ≤₹2.5 lakh, no income-tax payer or govt pensioner in family, ≤5 acres agricultural land, no four-wheeler The scheme was the centrepiece of the BJP campaign and of Congress's post-defeat commentary; BJP's swing (+7.6pp) was its best MP performance since 2013. This is consistent with, but does not on its own prove, a scheme effect — MP had no equivalent scheme in 2018 when BJP still narrowly lost the seat count, and Congress's Kamal Nath also ran a competing cash promise. PRS (Oct 2025): excluding UCT spending, Madhya Pradesh's revenue surplus would be 1.1% of GSDP; with it, 0.4% (2025-26 BE). The scheme is 6.4% of MP's revenue expenditure. Before Ladli Behna existed, RBI's June 2022 freebies table already put BJP-ruled MP fourth of nine states at 1.6% of GSDP (10.8% of revenue receipts, 28.8% of own tax revenue) — all of it a ₹21,000 cr electricity subsidy to farmers and domestic users, a long-standing subsidy rather than a new promise. RBI's 2022 'freebies' definition lumps legacy power subsidies (MP) together with new election promises (Punjab) — a definitional choice that inflates some states and not others. MP's position in any freebies ranking depends on whether pre-existing farm power subsidies are counted. Lokniti-CSDS post-poll (N=3,050, 18–24 Nov 2023): 80.4% of respondents said they or a female family member benefited from Ladli Behna (Q22: yes 2,454; no 403; don’t know 139; not eligible 54). BJP 48.6% and Congress 40.0% of valid votes after weighting to the actual result. 47.8% reported a Ladli Laxmi beneficiary. The public findings PDF as read carries no beneficiary × vote or gender × vote cross-tabulation. With coverage at ~80% of households, the scheme cannot discriminate BJP from Congress voters in the sample: it is a near-universal exposure, so any vote effect must be inferred from turnout or swing, not from a beneficiary/non-beneficiary contrast. Press consensus (Deccan Herald, 3 Dec 2023; ISAS, 6 Dec 2023) credited Ladli Behna as the ‘game-changer’ for the BJP’s 163-of-230 win; this is attribution by commentators, not an estimate. Counter-offer: Congress’s Kamal Nath promised ₹1,500/month (₹18,000/yr) for women on 2023-03-05 — both parties bid for the same constituency, which weakens any one-party ‘vote-buying’ reading. ₹260 crore of publicity in the months before the Nov 2023 election is roughly 9× the ₹28 crore spent publicising the youth stipend scheme in the same period Lokniti-CSDS MP post-poll 2023: 80.4% of respondents reported a female household member benefiting from Ladli Behna — coverage so near-universal that beneficiary status cannot discriminate BJP from Congress voters in the sample Lokniti-CSDS (as summarised by Oneindia): beneficiaries of Ladli Lakshmi/Ladli Behna 'were more inclined to vote for the BJP'; no gender cross-tab figures in the opened text Deccan Herald: BJP's women vote share rose from 43% to 50% (2018→2023); women turnout up 2 pts; state turnout 77.15% PRS: excluding UCT spending, MP's revenue surplus would be 1.1% of GSDP instead of 0.4% (2025-26 BE)

title: KALIA (Krushak Assistance for Livelihood and Income Augmentation)
summary: cultivators and landless agricultural labourers KALIA, launched four months before the 2019 poll, is one of the closest-in-time launches in this file, and BJD did win that election — but the same party's welfare architecture (KALIA plus later programmes) did not prevent a landslide loss five years later in 2024, when BJD lost 61 seats and its 24-year hold on power. A single scheme's timing is not a reliable predictor across a party's full run in office. CAG Report No 2 of 2024 (Odisha): implemented without beneficiary verification; the Bhulekh land-record database was not part of the exclusion logic; department itself found 14.08 lakh (27.58%) of the first 51.05 lakh ineligible (Rs 611.91 cr) and 9.76 lakh across phases; audit found a further 2.96 lakh (and 2.35 lakh in the first phase alone); Rs 782.26 cr paid to 12.72 lakh ineligible beneficiaries "with remote chances of recovery"; Rs 107.64 cr to 1.28 lakh accounts whose names differed from the beneficiaries; IT system built hastily without requirement study; only two of six components implemented. Government response (documented in the CAG exit conference and 2019 press): published lists, asked for voluntary refunds, formed panchayat/block/district committees to weed out fake beneficiaries. Timing: cabinet approval 21 Dec 2018, first cash Jan 2019, poll 11 Apr 2019 — a 3-month gap, and the payment universe (51 lakh) exceeded the eligible universe by a quarter. Innocent reading: a new scheme rushed for Rabi season under an admitted absence of khata/plot data (Scheme Implementation Committee, Jan 2019); over-inclusion, not targeted vote-buying, is what the audit describes. BJD still lost five seats and, five years later, the state.

title: Rythu Bandhu (Farmer's Investment Support Scheme)
summary: all landholding farmers, no acreage cap Rythu Bandhu ran uninterrupted through both the 2018 election (BRS won) and the 2023 election (BRS lost); its uncapped-per-acre design has been widely criticised in press commentary as favouring large landholders over tenant/landless farmers, though this file could not pin that critique to a specific fetched source this session, so it is recorded as analytic rather than documented/reported. A scheme continuing unchanged cannot, on its own, explain opposite outcomes in two different elections — the innocent/necessary-but-not-sufficient reading is that Rythu Bandhu's presence was necessary for BRS's 2018 coalition but insufficient against 2023 anti-incumbency, corruption allegations and Congress's competing guarantees. Inclusion error at the top: state estimates (TOI, Jan 2021) show ~13,000 farmers with 20–40 acres owning >3.19 lakh acres, eligible without cap; only 743 people returned money (up to ₹95 lakh) under the 'give it up' option; one season for large holders ≈ ₹150 cr. Principal Secretary (Agriculture) said payments 'depend on the financial condition of the state'. Telangana declared the largest off-budget borrowings of any state in 2021-22 — ₹35,258 cr, 53% of the 19-state total of ₹67,075 cr — falling to ₹2,697 cr by 2024-25; its outstanding guarantees were 15.1% of GSDP (Mar 2024), the highest ratio in India, with irrigation 37% of guarantees. The PRS table does not attribute any of this borrowing to Rythu Bandhu. A J-PAL-linked survey of the scheme was reported in 2019 (Wikipedia pointer to an archived Namasthe Telangana article); the archive copy could not be retrieved (connection reset), so no finding is recorded. IGIDR/IFROGS field study (2020): the scheme relies wholly on the 2017-18 land-record purification and pattadar passbooks; tenant and landless farmers are excluded by design; the entitlement covers ~10% of a small/marginal farmer's annual expenditure and ~6% of a medium/large farmer's; the 2019-20 budget provision (Rs 9,056 cr) fell short of the raised entitlement with no explanation, matching higher reported non-receipt for Rabi 2019; no grievance-redress forum. CAG (2021) cross-matched Rythu Bandhu land data (2018-20) with Aasara pension rolls: 12,152 pensioners from households holding >7.5 acres drew Rs 67.41 cr in undue pension; a further 2.04 lakh pensioners from 3–7.5 acre households drew Rs 1,150.71 cr whose eligibility could not be settled because wet/dry categorisation was missing — evidence that the Rythu Bandhu land base was usable for cross-checks that the state did not run. CM Revanth Reddy (INC) told the Assembly on 21 Dec 2024 that an estimated Rs 22,600 cr of the Rs 72,816 cr paid under BRS went to land not under cultivation. This is a government estimate stated by a political opponent of the scheme's authors; no audit report with this figure was opened. BRS working president K T Rama Rao replied that the Congress government was trying to evade implementing the scheme. Per-acre, uncapped design pays most to the largest landowners and nothing to tenants (IGIDR). Innocent reading: an input-support scheme keyed to land records is administratively simple and was delivered to 58 lakh farmers twice a year with low leakage relative to in-kind input subsidies.

summary: women aged 25-60, enrolled in Swasthya Sathi The 2026 hike is the closest-to-a-poll benefit increase in this entire file by announcement date (~2.5 months), timed identically to the 2021 pre-poll pattern that preceded a TMC win — yet in 2026 TMC lost to the BJP by a wide margin (BJP ~207/294 seats).
